{{Quote|He doesn't remember dying, Luke. He doesn't remember a switchover of any kind. And as much as I love&hellip;Nichos&hellip;as much as he loves me&hellip;I keep coming back to that. It isn't Nichos. He isn't human. He tries to be, and he wants to be, but flesh and bone have a logic of their own, Luke, and machinery just doesn't think the same way.|Cray Mingla, to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Children of the Jedi (novel)">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>}}
When the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Nichos Marr/Legends|Nichos Marr]] was stricken with the deadly [[Quannot's Syndrome]], his lover [[Cray Mingla]] attempted to transfer his life essence into a '''droid''' body using forbidden [[Ssi-ruu|Ssi-ruuk]] technology. The body had [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], as well as hands molded by the techs at the [[biomedical institute]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Unfortunately, as Mingla and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] determined later, Nichos's actual spirit and consciousness were not transferred. He was then merely a droid programmed to be like Nichos. Nichos, the droid, died aboard the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]]-size [[Dreadnaught/Legends|dreadnought]] ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'' alongside Mingla (who gave over her body to the then spiritual [[Callista Ming]]), when he ran through a defense system which destroyed much of his droid body's systems, giving his life so Skywalker, and all of the inhabitants of the targeted [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]], might live.
